chunks: And from the hadith of Ali ibn al-Ja'd, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Aqlah, Sammak and Husayn, all of them, from Jabir ibn Samrah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There will be after me twelve emirs.'

But Husayn said: 'Twelve caliphs.' Then he spoke something that I did not understand. And some of them said in his narration: 'So I asked my father.' And some of them said: 'So I asked the people,' and they said: 'He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve leaders predicted by the Prophet to succeed him?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani in *Kitab al-Ghayba*, serves as a foundational proof for the number of Imams in Shia theology, linking the Prophet's prediction directly to the Twelve Imams. While Sunni traditions often interpret 'emirs' or 'caliphs' broadly, Shia scholarship emphasizes the specific condition that all twelve must be from Quraysh, thereby validating the lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt. The variation in the final clause ('I did not understand') highlights the oral transmission nuances preserved in early hadith collections.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (15) Ali bin al-Ja’d narrated from Zuhayr from Ziyad bin Olaqa, Sammak and Hussayn and all from Jabir bin Samra that the Prophet (S) had said: “There will be twelve emirs after me.”

But Hussayn said: “There will be twelve caliphs…” Then the Prophet (S) said something that I could not understand. I asked some people and asked my father. He said that the Prophet (S) had said: “All of them are from Quraysh.”
